text:
A: Alright! Hello, hello. Can you see me?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Very loud, actually.
A: Ha, sorry, Natalie says I don't have a volume knob. I'm Tendai.
B: Leanne. I'm in Stockport. And before you say it, it's not Manchester.
A: I wasn't gonna say nothing! I'm in Gloucester. Nobody ever argues about Gloucester, you know.
B: Nobody's ever heard of Gloucester.
A: Ah, that's harsh! We've got a cathedral. They did Harry Potter there. Er, so what do you do?
B: Graphic designer. Part-time, at a little print and signage place. Menus, leaflets, shop signs. It's not exactly glamorous. Last week a café owner asked me for Comic Sans "but nicer." That's my life.
A: Comic Sans but nicer. Is that a thing?
B: No, it's not a thing, that's the point. I told him it'd look like a 2009 Facebook page. He went quiet. And you're a sparky, aren't you? I could tell from the polo. You look exactly like my Gavin when he gets in.
A: Your fella's an electrician? Ah, brilliant. Tell him from me, the price of copper cable right now, it's criminal.
B: Oh, I know. I hear about the copper. I hear about it every night over tea.
A: Then you know my pain! Yeah, I'm self-employed, rewires mostly, consumer units, kitchens. Fifty-odd hours a week. And my van heater's been broken since November, so I'm sat there in the mornings in my coat like a, er, like a fish finger in a freezer.
B: Get it fixed, then.
A: That's what Natalie says! I'll do it when it calms down. It never calms down.
B: Gavin's the same. Fixes everyone's house, ours has a light switch hanging off the wall.
A: Ha! That's the law, man. Electrician's house, nothing works. So you do your own art as well? I saw the prints in your picture, on the string.
B: Yeah, that's the stuff I actually care about. Screen prints, risograph zines. I sell them at craft fairs and online. I sold out of one at a fair in Manchester last month, which, honestly, I was dead chuffed about. Client work just pays the rent, do you know what I mean? And I've got rheumatoid arthritis, so I can only do so many hours. I'd rather spend them on things I rate.
A: Ah, sorry to hear that. That must be hard, yeah.
B: It's fine. Well, it's not fine, but. I used to skate roller derby. My name was Moth to a Flame. Then the joints went.
A: Roller derby! Proper tough. I play five-a-side, but that's just old men falling over, you know. Every other Wednesday, I turn up, I run for ten minutes, I'm done.
B: Let me guess. United?
A: Arsenal! Since I was a kid in Harare, watching on the telly. Lifelong.
B: I find all that stuff a bit tedious, to be honest. Gavin's County, so I go for the pies.
A: The pies are the best part anyway, so you're not wrong. I go to Gloucester Rugby sometimes, I don't understand the rules, I just shout when everyone shouts.
B: That's basically how I watch County.
A: See, we're the same! Hey, have you got a cat? I saw a grey one on the cabinet.
B: That's Moth. She knocks everything off my desk. Pens, mugs, a whole print once.
A: Ha, a critic! Sounds like —
